note: Physics-reactive obstacles. These export as NON-STATIC SDF models with mass, inertia and surface parameters; Gazebo's solver produces all of their motion. Nothing here is keyframed. Blender's own rigid-body system does not export -- sar_physics_preview.py only arms a viewport preview.

BARREL.note: Part-full steel drum. Tips, then rolls.

CRATE.note: Supply crate. Slides and tumbles, does not roll.

PALLET.note: Flat and low -- a genuine LiDAR ambiguity: the robot must decide whether to drive over it.

CONE.note: Traffic cone. Light enough to knock flat without stopping the robot -- tests whether contact is detected at all.

PANEL.note: Loose sheet metal. Low friction, slides a long way.

PIPE.note: Loose pipe lying across the ground. Rolls perpendicular to its axis and not at all along it.

JERRYCAN.note: Fuel can. Small enough to vanish under a bumper.

BIN.note: Wheeled bin. Tall, light, topples easily.

clusters.note: Staging yard on the apron. First movable things the robot sees, on flat ground where a failed push is unambiguous.
Cones narrowing the base gate. Directly on the exit path -- the robot meets these in the first ten metres of every run.
Street furniture strewn across Urban Street A, the alternative when Street C is blocked by the overturned truck.
Inside the 7.5 m canyon between URB_001 and URB_002. Narrows an already tight corridor, and the walls leave nowhere to swing wide -- the robot either pushes through or backs out.
Loading yard outside the warehouse roller door.
Loose pipe and sheet at the collapse-field margin, beside the rubble bypass. Rolling pipe on sloped debris is the nastiest case here: it moves after the robot has passed it.
Debris washed onto the flood plain. Scattered, low contrast against mud.
Dropped stores beside the desert track. Sand gives low friction under both the prop and the robot.
Forward staging point on the forest track, under canopy shadow.
